newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares pulled up by Vilniaus, Hermis.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares pulled up by Vilniaus, Hermis.

text.p: Vilniaus and Hermis Banks were in the spotlight again on Lithuania's bourse on Wednesday, giving hope that the struggling market may pick up some steam after weeks of summer-induced inactivity.
The official group index rose by 14.57 points to 913.71 while the group A index inched up 1.04 points to 1872.2.
The turnover on the central market was 434,000 litas and 1.9 million litas was registered in block trades.
Dealers said that low prices, especially for Hermis Bank, seemed to be bringing buyers back to the market.
Hermis Bank rose to 198.2 million litas from 195 litas in trade of 84,000 litas on the central market.
It also saw 834,000 litas worth of its shares change hands in block trades with prices ranging from 195 to 197 litas.
The bank announced on Wednesday after the morning price fix that its first half profit was 14.3 million litas and that it saw no reason to revise its forecast of a '97 profit of 40.6 million litas.
The reaction of dealers to the result was mixed, but most remained bullish about the stock and predicted that it would post further gains.
Vilniaus Bank also rose, adding two percent to 240 litas in central market trade of 84,000 litas. It turned over 460,000 litas in block trades at the same price.
Dealers are expecting its results, due out soon, to be promising.
Rokishkis Cheese rose to 41 litas from 39 litas in trade of 82,000 litas on the central market. It turned over 382,000 litas in the block trade at prices ranging from 40 to 40.5 litas.
The secondary T-bill market turned over 385,000 litas.
